docs.text: Driver TLE92466ED Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the Infineon TLE92466ED six-channel low-side solenoid driver. It starts the chip, regulates each coil current with the chip's own controller and dither, reads the current feedback and the diagnosis, and checks every SPI reply, on any MCU. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that brings the bus up and moves 32-bit frames; it does the rest: the reset and start-up sequence, the operation states, the frame CRC, the one-frame reply pipeline, unit conversion, fault latching and bounded waits. Six-channel low-side solenoid driver TLE92466ED Infineon Function Six low-side channels with integrated MOSFETs and shunts; each regulates its average coil current Current 0 to 1.5 A per channel, 15-bit setpoint, 1 % accuracy; 1.8 A with dither; 2.43 A from a parallel pair (2.7 A range) Control Integrating current controller with a PWM frequency controller (110 Hz to 4 kHz), dither generator, direct drive from SPI or the DRV0/DRV1 pins Diagnosis Open load, short to ground and overcurrent in ON and OFF state, overtemperature, supply and clock monitors Interface SPI mode 1, up to 8 MHz; 32-bit frames with CRC-8 SAE J1850; SPI watchdog Supply VDD 4.5 V to 5.5 V, VIO 3.3 V or 5 V, VBAT 6 V to 18 V What you get ¶ One object per chip. TLE92466ED<YourPort> takes a reference to your port and does no I/O until EnsureInitialized() . See API guide . Errors you can act on. Every call returns Result<T> with an Error such as NoDevice , MissionBlocked or CriticalFault . See API guide . Replies proven before they are used. CRC, reply width, R/W echo, status and an anchor read in every access: a stuck, looped-back or out-of-step bus is an error, never data. See Architecture . Datasheet defaults. Config{} holds the chip's reset values, with units in the field names, plus a current-control preset. See Configuration . Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class checked by a concept: the bus hooks and a delay, plus optional RESN, EN, DRV, FAULTN and logging hooks found at compile time. See Porting . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI. The host tests build with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti . See Contract . Tested without hardware, honest about it. Host tests run the driver against a protocol model of the chip; what only a bench can confirm is listed in Status and limitations . API guide ¶ The driver's API by task, with code that compiles: start, operation states, channels, feedback, faults, the watchdog, errors and shut-down. Section numbers refer to the datasheet, Rev. 1.2. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Infineon IFX-ntz1491827137291 1.2: Reset State, Config Mode, Mission Mode and Critical Fault: 4.3.1 TDS_IC Operation states; Figure 4, p. 19 Channel modes and the measurement period: 4.4 Channel modes, p. 21 Parallel channel pairs: 4.5.2 TDS_Parallel channel operation, p. 22 Integrating current controller, Autolimit and the PWM frequency controller: 4.6.2 Integrating Current Controller (ICC); Equations 4, 5, p. 24 Setpoint range and accuracy: 4.6.3 Electrical characteristics current control, Table 14, p. 28 Dither waveform and its update: 4.7.1 TDS_Dither configuration; 4.7.2 TDS_Dither parameter update; Equations 6 to 9, p. 29 ON-state and OFF-state diagnosis: 4.9.1 TDS_Overview; Figures 14, 15, p. 32 Open load or short to ground, thresholds and warning: 4.9.2 TDS_Open Load/Short to Ground (OLSG); 4.9.3 TDS_OLSG Warning, p. 34 Overcurrent and the OFF-state overcurrent check: 4.9.6 TDS_Overcurrent (OC); Equation 17, p. 38 Register and OTP ECC, the self-test: 4.9.7 TDS_Register/OTP ECC; 4.9.8 TDS_Built in Self Test (BIST), p. 39 Average current, duty cycle and VBAT feedback: 4.10.2 TDS_Average feedback values; Equations 18 to 22, p. 41 Feedback freeze and update: 4.10.5 TDS_Update/Freeze Mechanism; Figure 22, p. 43 Overtemperature and the temperature feedback: 4.11.1 TDS_Overtemperature protection; Equation 32, p. 45 SPI watchdog: 5.2.2 TDS_SPI watchdog; Equation 33, p. 50 FB_STAT, the status summary: 5.3.2.21 Feedback Status Register, p. 77 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The shape of the API ¶ Group Calls Lifecycle EnsureInitialized() , IsInitialized() , Deinitialize() , HardwareReset() Configuration ApplyConfig() , GetConfig() , ConfigureChannel() , SetParallel() Operation state EnterMissionMode() , EnterConfigMode() , IsMissionMode() , ReadChannelControl() Channels SetCurrent() , GetCurrentSetpoint() , EnableChannel() , DisableChannel() , SetEnabledChannels() , GetEnabledChannels() , SetDither() , StartOvercurrentCheck() , SetDrivePin() Feedback ReadChannelFeedback() , ReadSupply() Diagnosis ReadStatus() , ReadFaults() , ClearFaults() , ClearChannelFaults() , GetLatchedFaults() , ClearLatchedFaults() , GetStartupFaults() , ReadFaultPin() , ReadPinStatus() , RunBist() Watchdog ReloadWatchdog() Identification GetIcVersion() , ReadChipId() , tle92466ed::GetDriverVersion() Raw access ReadRegister() , GetLastReply() , GetLastCriticalFault() , GetBusDiagnostics() , IsResetWatchArmed() Every call that touches the chip returns Result<T> : check ok() (or the bool conversion) and read value , or read error . Result is [[nodiscard]] , so an unchecked call is a compiler warning. Setters take a trailing Verify verify = Verify::None : Verify::ReadBack reads the written register back (two more frames each) and returns WriteMismatch when the chip did not take the value. Start and enter Mission Mode ¶ tle92466ed :: Error BringUp ( Driver & driver ) { // The one entry point: starts the chip on the first call, then returns Ok with no I/O. After a // failure the next call starts again from the beginning. It ends in Config Mode. if ( const auto r = driver . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { std :: printf ( "TLE92466ED init: %s 
 " , tle92466ed :: ToString ( r . error )); return r . error ; } return driver . EnterMissionMode (). error ; // MissionBlocked: a supply, clock or watchdog fault } The constructor stores the port and the configuration ( Config{} unless you pass one) and does no I/O. EnsureInitialized() is the one way to start the chip ( Contract lists its steps); it ends in Config Mode with every channel off. Once it has succeeded it returns Ok at once with no I/O, so a caller can call it before every use. After a failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again. The chip has four operation states (section 4.3.1, Figure 4): State What works The driver Reset Nothing; registers return to their reset values RESN low in EnsureInitialized() and HardwareReset() Config Mode Registers; every channel off; MODE, GLOBAL_CONFIG, CLK_DIV, CH_PAR and SFF_BIST writable only here EnsureInitialized() ends here; EnterConfigMode() ; ApplyConfig() , ConfigureChannel() , SetParallel() , RunBist() Mission Mode Channels switch; their diagnosis runs; EN_CH settable only here EnterMissionMode() ; EnableChannel() , StartOvercurrentCheck() Critical Fault Every reply is a critical fault frame; FAULTN low A critical fault frame confirmed by a second one is CriticalFault : EN low, the driver uninitialised; EnsureInitialized() (with RESN) or a power cycle leaves it EnterMissionMode() checks the entry conditions of Figure 4 first and returns MissionBlocked , writing nothing, while INIT_DONE is 0 or one fails: FB_STAT (SPI watchdog, clock, central temperature, VDD, VIO, VBAT or an internal supply), the DIAG_ERR_CHGR and DIAG_WARN_CHGR groups FB_STAT flags (a channel OTE or OTW) and GLOBAL_DIAG2 (REG_ECC_ERR). VPRE_OV blocks entry too, a fail-safe choice beyond Figure 4. Then it drives EN high, sets OP_MODE and reads CH_CTRL back, always: a chip that refused is MissionBlocked , and IsMissionMode() says what the chip did. A supply, clock or watchdog fault later drops the chip back to Config Mode on its own and clears every EN_CH (sections 4.1.2, 4.2.2, 5.2.2); a channel fault clears that channel's EN_CH (4.9.2 to 4.9.6). The driver never writes CH_CTRL from a copy the chip may have changed: every enable change reads CH_CTRL first. Drive a channel ¶ tle92466ed :: Error Energise ( Driver & driver , uint32_t microamps ) { const auto set = driver . SetCurrent ( Channel :: Ch0 , microamps ); // checked, never clamped if ( ! set ) { return set . error ; // InvalidArgument above 1.5 A, or with dither above 1.8 A } std :: printf ( "programmed %lu uA 
 " , static_cast < unsigned long > ( set . value )); // TARGET rounding return driver . EnableChannel ( Channel :: Ch0 , tle92466ed :: Verify :: ReadBack ). error ; } SetCurrent() sets the average current of the integrating current controller (sections 4.6.1, 4.6.2). The value is checked against the operating range of Table 14 and refused, never clamped: up to 1.5 A, up to 1.8 A with the configured dither amplitude, and above the dither amplitude when it is not 0 (section 4.7.1). The master of a parallel pair takes up to 2.43 A with dither ( kMaxParallelSetpointUa : Table 14's 2.7 A includes the overshoot, and the driver keeps the single channel's 90 % headroom), and its TARGET step doubles to 122 µA (section 4.5.2). SetParallel() sets the master's setpoint to 0 when it joins a pair. The call returns the current actually programmed, rounded to the TARGET step; GetCurrentSetpoint() returns it with no I/O. Setpoints may be written in either state: the channel switches once it is enabled in Mission Mode. EnableChannel() , DisableChannel() and SetEnabledChannels() read CH_CTRL, then write it whole with only the EN_CH bits they name changed: enabling one channel never switches another off, a channel a fault switched off is never switched back on, and OP_MODE is never set (only EnterMissionMode() sets it). An enable that finds the chip back in Config Mode is MissionBlocked . Switching off never depends on that read: when it fails, a disable (or any mask that only clears) still writes CH_CTRL from the copy with the channels cleared and returns the read's error, and EnterConfigMode() drives EN low whatever the SPI result. Section 5.2.1 does not say whether a write's reply carries CH_CTRL before or after the write, so the copy holds an EN_CH or OP_MODE bit only when both the value written and the reply have it: GetEnabledChannels() can under-report a channel that is on until the next read, never report one that is off. Channels the driver wrote on that a validated read of CH_CTRL (the read before every channel call, or Verify::ReadBack ) finds off are logged and kept in GetDroppedChannels() until ClearDroppedChannels() or the next start; a refused EnterMissionMode() drives EN low again. A channel must be declared loaded in its ChannelConfig and must not be a slave. The chip keeps a channel switched off by a fault off until its flags are cleared and EN_CH is set again (sections 4.9.2 to 4.9.6); Verify::ReadBack finds such a channel as WriteMismatch , and the driver's copy then shows it off. SetDither() changes a channel's dither while it runs: DITHER_CLK_DIV takes effect at once, DITHER_STEP and DITHER_CTRL at the next dither period after the DITHER_CTRL write (section 4.7.2). The dither period is also the feedback measurement period in current control and direct drive (section 4.4.2). Read the feedback ¶ void SampleCurrent ( Driver & driver ) { const auto fb = driver . ReadChannelFeedback ( Channel :: Ch0 ); // freeze, read, release (4.10.5) if ( fb . error == tle92466ed :: Error :: NotReady ) { return ; // no new measurement period yet: never a 0 mA reading } if ( fb ) { std :: printf ( "%ld uA, duty %lu/10000 
 " , static_cast < long > ( fb . value . average_current_ua ), static_cast < unsigned long > ( fb . value . duty_permyriad )); } } ReadChannelFeedback() reads one measurement period under the freeze of section 4.10.5: average current (signed, the pair's sum on a master), duty cycle, VBAT, the measurement period, the minimum and maximum current and PWM period, and the fast-feedback counters. With no new values since the last read it returns NotReady after two frames; with no measurement period at all (TP_MANT = 0, as with a dither clock of 0) it returns NotReady too, never a current of 0. The conversions use f_SYS of the configuration. ReadSupply() reads VIO, VDD, VBAT and the central temperature (±20 °C uncalibrated, Table 16). Faults ¶ void ServiceFaults ( Driver & driver ) { const auto f = driver . ReadFaults (); // every diagnosis register, ORed into the latch if ( ! f || ! f . value . Any ()) { return ; } const tle92466ed :: ChannelFaults ch0 = f . value . Of ( Channel :: Ch0 ); if ( ch0 . open_load || ch0 . short_to_ground || ch0 . olsg ) { std :: printf ( "CH0 load fault 
 " ); } // The chip keeps a faulted channel off until its flags are cleared and EN_CH is set again. if ( driver . ClearChannelFaults ( Channel :: Ch0 )) { ( void ) driver . EnableChannel ( Channel :: Ch0 ); } } Call I/O What it gives ReadStatus() 2 frames FB_STAT: INIT_DONE, the global faults, and a bit per channel group with an error or warning ReadFaults() 18 frames GLOBAL_DIAG0..2, DIAG_ERR_CHGR0..2, DIAG_WARN_CHGR0..2 as Faults ; Has() and Of() decode them ClearFaults() 18 frames, 2 more per register with a flag (4 with OC or OTP_ECC_ERR) Every register read and latched, then exactly the flags read cleared: rwh flags by a 1, rw flags by a 0, OC and OTP_ECC_ERR twice; OTP_VIRGIN never ClearChannelFaults(ch) 4 frames, 2 more per write The group read and latched (both channels), then this channel's flags that read 1 cleared GetLatchedFaults() none Every flag any read of a diagnosis register saw since ClearLatchedFaults() GetStartupFaults() none The diagnosis registers as the start-up found them, before it cleared them ReadFaultPin() GpioRead() FAULTN: low on Critical Fault, RESN low or an unmasked fault ReadPinStatus() 2 frames PIN_STAT: DRV0, DRV1, EN, the internal fault state and the FAULTN level The diagnosis runs only in Mission Mode (section 4.9.1). In ON state the shunt current shows an open load or a short to ground only together, as OLSG, below the open-load threshold; in OFF state (EN_CH set with setpoint 0, or a setpoint with EN_CH cleared) the current sources of Figure 14 tell OL from SG. Use both. OLSG_WARN_CHK_NOK is cleared by reading DIAG_WARN_CHGR (section 4.9.3): the latch keeps it. StartOvercurrentCheck() runs the OFF-state overcurrent check of section 4.9.6 once, on a channel that is off with setpoint 0 and not asked on since the last read of CH_CTRL (after a refused enable, call ReadChannelControl() first); read the result with ReadFaults() after t_OCon. The channel then stays enabled with setpoint 0, the OFF-state diagnosis condition. RunBist() runs the safety flip-flop self-test in Config Mode (section 4.9.8) and clears the REG_ECC_ERR it sets on purpose. The SPI watchdog ¶ void ControlTick ( Driver & driver ) { // With Config::spi_watchdog, a missed reload ends Mission Mode and turns every channel off. if ( const auto r = driver . ReloadWatchdog (); ! r ) { std :: printf ( "watchdog reload: %s 
 " , tle92466ed :: ToString ( r . error )); } } With Config::spi_watchdog , the chip counts WD_TIME down at f_SYS / 2^14 (0.585 ms per count) and, at 0, sets SPI_WD_ERR, ends Mission Mode and switches every channel off (section 5.2.2). EnsureInitialized() writes Config::watchdog_reload to WD_RELOAD before it enables the watchdog, since the reset value of 1 would expire at once. ReloadWatchdog() writes it again; call it faster than the timeout. WD_TIME is 11 bits: at most 2047 counts, 1.198 s. After an expiry, a reload clears SPI_WD_ERR, ClearFaults() the latched flag, and EnterMissionMode() works again. Handle errors ¶ const char * Describe ( tle92466ed :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case tle92466ed :: Error :: Bus : case tle92466ed :: Error :: NoDevice : return "check SPI wiring, VIO and the chip select" ; case tle92466ed :: Error :: CriticalFault : return "internal supply or clock fault: reset the chip" ; case tle92466ed :: Error :: Crc : case tle92466ed :: Error :: ReplyMismatch : return "signal integrity: lower SCK, check CSN high time" ; default : return tle92466ed :: ToString ( e ); } } Signal Meaning What to do Error::Bus The port failed a transfer, a pin write or the bus bring-up Check the port and the wiring; retry Error::NoDevice MISO stuck low or high, or MOSI looped back VIO, SO, CSN and the chip's supplies Error::Crc , ReplyMismatch , FrameRejected A frame was corrupted, lost or ignored SPI mode 1, the clock, CSN high time; a shared bus lock Error::Timeout INIT_DONE never read 1, or the self-test did not finish VDD, RESN, the clock source Error::DeviceIdMismatch ICVID is not a TLE92466ED The part, the chip select Error::DeviceFault OTP not programmed, or an internal bus fault Replace the part Error::CriticalFault Internal supply or clock fault, confirmed by a second frame; EN is low GetLastCriticalFault() , then EnsureInitialized() (RESN) Error::MissionBlocked A fault holds the chip in Config Mode, or it left Mission Mode on its own ReadFaults() , fix the cause, ClearFaults() , EnterMissionMode() Error::WrongState The call needs the other state, the channel is a slave, or an earlier write failed and the chip may hold either value (see the contract, "Ambiguous writes") Change state first; after a failed write, repeat it or ReadChannelControl() Error::WriteMismatch The chip did not take a write A latched fault, the state, or a lost frame: read the faults Error::NotReady No feedback to report Wait one measurement period; configure the dither clock Error::UnexpectedReset The chip reset behind the driver's back; EN is low EnsureInitialized() configures it again Error::Unsupported The port lacks the hook Add GpioSet() or GpioRead() Every value is on the Contract page. tle92466ed::ToString() names an error for a log. Raw access and counters ¶ For bring-up and fault finding (handbook KB-CPP-129): Call I/O What it gives ReadRegister(address) 2 frames, no retry The 16 or 22 data bits of any register of Tables 19 and 24; a diagnosis register read here feeds the latch, and DIAG_WARN_CHGR clears OLSG_WARN_CHK_NOK on the chip GetLastReply() none The last 32-bit word clocked in as a reply, by any call GetLastCriticalFault() none The flags byte of the last critical fault frame GetBusDiagnostics() none Frames sent, reads retried, replies rejected, resyncs GetDroppedChannels() none Channels the chip switched off on its own, bit x for channel x; ClearDroppedChannels() empties it IsResetWatchArmed() none Whether every FB_STAT anchor checks for a chip reset Shut down ¶ void PowerDown ( Driver & driver ) { if ( auto r = driver . Deinitialize (); ! r ) { // Config Mode, every channel off, EN low std :: printf ( "TLE92466ED shutdown write failed: %s 
 " , tle92466ed :: ToString ( r . error )); } } After Deinitialize() every call returns NotInitialized until the next EnsureInitialized() , which starts the chip again from the beginning: Deinitialize() then EnsureInitialized() is also the recovery after a fault. Next: Configuration .

The value is checked against the operating range of Table 14 and refused, never clamped: up to 1.5 A, up to 1.8 A with the configured dither amplitude, and above the dither amplitude when it is not 0 (section 4.7.1). The master of a parallel pair takes up to 2.43 A with dither ( kMaxParallelSetpointUa : Table 14's 2.7 A includes the overshoot, and the driver keeps the single channel's 90 % headroom), and its TARGET step doubles to 122 µA (section 4.5.2). SetParallel() sets the master's setpoint to 0 when it joins a pair. The call returns the current actually programmed, rounded to the TARGET step; GetCurrentSetpoint() returns it with no I/O. Setpoints may be written in either state: the channel switches once it is enabled in Mission Mode. EnableChannel() , DisableChannel() and SetEnabledChannels() read CH_CTRL, then write it whole with only the EN_CH bits they name changed: enabling one channel never switches another off, a channel a fault switched off is never switched back on, and OP_MODE is never set (only EnterMissionMode() sets it). An enable that finds the chip back in Config Mode is MissionBlocked . Switching off never depends on that read: when it fails, a disable (or any mask that only clears) still writes CH_CTRL from the copy with the channels cleared and returns the read's error, and EnterConfigMode() drives EN low whatever the SPI result. Section 5.2.1 does not say whether a write's reply carries CH_CTRL before or after the write, so the copy holds an EN_CH or OP_MODE bit only when both the value written and the reply have it: GetEnabledChannels() can under-report a channel that is on until the next read, never report one that is off. Channels the driver wrote on that a validated read of CH_CTRL (the read before every channel call, or Verify::ReadBack ) finds off are logged and kept in GetDroppedChannels() until ClearDroppedChannels() or the next start; a refused EnterMissionMode() drives EN low again. A channel must be declared loaded in its ChannelConfig and must not be a slave. The chip keeps a channel switched off by a fault off until its flags are cleared and EN_CH is set again (sections 4.9.2 to 4.9.6); Verify::ReadBack finds such a channel as WriteMismatch , and the driver's copy then shows it off. SetDither() changes a channel's dither while it runs: DITHER_CLK_DIV takes effect at once, DITHER_STEP and DITHER_CTRL at the next dither period after the DITHER_CTRL write (section 4.7.2). The dither period is also the feedback measurement period in current control and direct drive (section 4.4.2).

docs.text: void ControlTick ( Driver & driver ) { // With Config::spi_watchdog, a missed reload ends Mission Mode and turns every channel off. if ( const auto r = driver . ReloadWatchdog (); ! r ) { std :: printf ( "watchdog reload: %s \n " , tle92466ed :: ToString ( r . error )); } } With Config::spi_watchdog , the chip counts WD_TIME down at f_SYS / 2^14 (0.585 ms per count) and, at 0, sets SPI_WD_ERR, ends Mission Mode and switches every channel off (section 5.2.2). EnsureInitialized() writes Config::watchdog_reload to WD_RELOAD before it enables the watchdog, since the reset value of 1 would expire at once. docs.text: Changelog ¶ What changed in each release of the driver. Entries under Breaking need source changes in code that used the affected API. [Unreleased] ¶ Changed ¶ The repository moved to kokeb-labs-drivers; URLs follow. Hardware page: the pinout, the block diagram and the application circuit are now figures drawn from docs/hardware.yml , which also generates the pin table (replacing the hand-written one) and the parts table. Every pin, block and part cites the datasheet section and page; values the datasheet does not give are marked as not confirmed. kokeb-docs hardware --kicad-netlist exports the circuit. Synced with the driver template: tools/preflight.sh runs clang-tidy over every file CI lints, as CI does, and the hardware-lessons review adds the switch-off, channel-in-doubt and fuzz-skip lessons. [0.1.0] - 2026-11-09 ¶ Added ¶ Driver : the first version of the Infineon TLE92466ED driver (datasheet Rev. 1.2): start-up with the RESN pulse or t_POR, INIT_DONE, the ICVID identity and the start-up faults reported and cleared; Config and Mission Mode; per-channel mode, current setpoint, integrating current controller, PWM frequency controller, dither, slew rate and diagnosis; parallel pairs; channel enables written from a fresh read of CH_CTRL; feedback under the freeze of section 4.10.5; supply and temperature readings; every diagnosis register, a fault latch and the clears; the OFF-state overcurrent check; the self-test; the SPI watchdog; the external clock; raw register reads. Protocol : 32-bit frames with CRC-8 SAE J1850 and a two-frame access with an anchor read that checks every reply (CRC, width, R/W echo, status, stuck and looped-back lines, repeated words), bounded retries of reads, resynchronisation after a failure, reset detection. Safe switch-off : a disable writes even when the CH_CTRL read fails, EnterConfigMode() and a refused EnterMissionMode() drive EN low whatever happens on the bus, and GetDroppedChannels() reports the channels the chip switched off on its own, from validated reads only. The CH_CTRL copy never reports a channel on that is off, whether a write's reply carries the register before or after the write (section 5.2.1); the host tests run under both readings. A write whose reply failed may have taken effect: every copy the driver decides on without I/O then holds the more dangerous value or is unknown, and a guard on an unknown value returns WrongState with nothing sent ( docs/contract.md , "Ambiguous writes"). docs.text: Contract ¶ What the TLE92466ED driver promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Infineon IFX-ntz1491827137291 1.2: The reply pipeline, frames and reply status: 5.2.1 TDS_Data flow; 5.2.3 SPI frame definition, p. 50 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. A change to anything here is a breaking change, listed under Breaking in the changelog . Promises ¶ The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() is the only way to start the driver. Its first call checks the stored configuration ( InvalidArgument , nothing sent), brings the bus up, resets the chip (RESN when the port has GpioSet() , otherwise it waits t_POR), waits for INIT_DONE, checks ICVID, puts the chip in Config Mode with every channel off, reports and clears the faults it finds, and only then writes the configuration. On any failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again from the beginning; once it has succeeded, later calls return Ok with no I/O. Every call that touches the chip returns Error::NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() succeeds. No call initialises or resets the chip as a side effect. ApplyConfig() and ConfigureChannel() before the start only store the configuration. Every port failure propagates as Error::Bus ; a failed call returns T{} , never a stale or zero value. A reply is used only after every check of Architecture passed. A read is repeated at most Config::max_retries times; a write never. A call sends only the frames the datasheet needs; a read-back costs two frames per register and is asked for per call with Verify::ReadBack . The start-up checks (INIT_DONE, ICVID, GLOBAL_CONFIG read back, the reset watch) are unconditional. A setter checks its arguments and the operation state before any I/O ( InvalidArgument , WrongState : nothing sent), reads CH_CTRL before it writes it, writes it whole with only what it names changed, never sets an EN_CH bit it was not asked for nor OP_MODE (only EnterMissionMode() does). The copy can only under-report: after a write it holds an EN_CH or OP_MODE bit only when the value written and the reply both have it (after a failed write, the value and the previous copy), whichever contents the reply carries (section 5.2.1). A confirmed critical fault and a detected reset drive EN low and leave the driver uninitialised. Switching off never depends on a read: a clear-only enable change writes even when the CH_CTRL read failed, EnterConfigMode() drives EN low whatever the SPI result, and a refused EnterMissionMode() drives EN low again. A write whose reply failed may have taken effect (see "Ambiguous writes" below): every value the driver decides on without I/O then holds the more dangerous of the two, or is unknown, and a guard on an unknown value returns WrongState with nothing sent. Switching off and a setpoint of 0 are never refused: SetEnabledChannels() keeps an unknown channel that is already on as the chip has it and still switches the others off. Diagnosis flags are read and latched before they are cleared, and only the flags read are cleared. Every wait is bounded: INIT_DONE by Config::init_timeout_us , the self-test by kBistTimeoutUs , each poll by kPollIntervalUs . Config{} equals the datasheet reset values; a channel the configuration does not declare loaded cannot be enabled, runs no OFF-state diagnosis and never reaches FAULTN. A missing DelayUs() is a compile error; a missing GpioSet() gives Error::Unsupported from HardwareReset() and SetDrivePin() ; a missing GpioRead() from ReadFaultPin() ; a missing Log() logs nothing. A misdeclared hook is a compile error. Deinitialize() leaves the chip in Config Mode with every channel off and EN low. docs.text: The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() is the only way to start the driver. Its first call checks the stored configuration ( InvalidArgument , nothing sent), brings the bus up, resets the chip (RESN when the port has GpioSet() , otherwise it waits t_POR), waits for INIT_DONE, checks ICVID, puts the chip in Config Mode with every channel off, reports and clears the faults it finds, and only then writes the configuration. On any failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again from the beginning; once it has succeeded, later calls return Ok with no I/O. Every call that touches the chip returns Error::NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() succeeds. No call initialises or resets the chip as a side effect. ApplyConfig() and ConfigureChannel() before the start only store the configuration. Every port failure propagates as Error::Bus ; a failed call returns T{} , never a stale or zero value. A reply is used only after every check of Architecture passed. A read is repeated at most Config::max_retries times; a write never. A call sends only the frames the datasheet needs; a read-back costs two frames per register and is asked for per call with Verify::ReadBack . The start-up checks (INIT_DONE, ICVID, GLOBAL_CONFIG read back, the reset watch) are unconditional. A setter checks its arguments and the operation state before any I/O ( InvalidArgument , WrongState : nothing sent), reads CH_CTRL before it writes it, writes it whole with only what it names changed, never sets an EN_CH bit it was not asked for nor OP_MODE (only EnterMissionMode() does). The copy can only under-report: after a write it holds an EN_CH or OP_MODE bit only when the value written and the reply both have it (after a failed write, the value and the previous copy), whichever contents the reply carries (section 5.2.1). A confirmed critical fault and a detected reset drive EN low and leave the driver uninitialised. Switching off never depends on a read: a clear-only enable change writes even when the CH_CTRL read failed, EnterConfigMode() drives EN low whatever the SPI result, and a refused EnterMissionMode() drives EN low again. A write whose reply failed may have taken effect (see "Ambiguous writes" below): every value the driver decides on without I/O then holds the more dangerous of the two, or is unknown, and a guard on an unknown value returns WrongState with nothing sent. Switching off and a setpoint of 0 are never refused: SetEnabledChannels() keeps an unknown channel that is already on as the chip has it and still switches the others off. Diagnosis flags are read and latched before they are cleared, and only the flags read are cleared. Every wait is bounded: INIT_DONE by Config::init_timeout_us , the self-test by kBistTimeoutUs , each poll by kPollIntervalUs . Config{} equals the datasheet reset values; a channel the configuration does not declare loaded cannot be enabled, runs no OFF-state diagnosis and never reaches FAULTN. A missing DelayUs() is a compile error; a missing GpioSet() gives Error::Unsupported from HardwareReset() and SetDrivePin() ; a missing GpioRead() from ReadFaultPin() ; a missing Log() logs nothing. A misdeclared hook is a compile error. Deinitialize() leaves the chip in Config Mode with every channel off and EN low.

docs.text: Examples ¶ One folder per platform under examples/ , each with its own port, built by CI on every pull request. The driver itself has no platform code; Platforms lists what exists. Host ¶ examples/host/ runs the driver on any PC against a simulated TLE92466ED, through the host port host_tle92466ed_port.hpp . No hardware: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example && cmake --build build-example && ./build-example/tle92466ed_host_example The host tests build it with warnings as errors and run it (CTest tle92466ed_host_example ). Control pins ¶ The driver drives RESN, EN, DRV0 and DRV1 only through the optional GpioSet() hook of your port, with logical levels ( GpioSignal::ACTIVE on RESN means "in reset", which your port writes as a low level), and reads FAULTN through the optional GpioRead() hook. Their idle levels, which your port drives before it enables each output: Pin Idle level Why RESN Low, ACTIVE (in reset) Every register at its reset value and every channel off until the driver starts the chip EN Low, INACTIVE Every channel off; the driver raises it in EnterMissionMode() and lowers it in EnterConfigMode() DRV0, DRV1 Low, INACTIVE A direct-drive channel stays off until the application drives the pin CSN High The SPI driver's job; the chip ignores the bus while CSN is high Without GpioSet() , tie RESN and EN high (through a resistor) and DRVx low: EnsureInitialized() then waits t_POR instead of pulsing RESN and writes every register, since the chip may keep what an earlier run wrote, and HardwareReset() and SetDrivePin() return Error::Unsupported . docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( tle92466ed_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-tle92466ed.git external/driver-tle92466ed git submodule update --init external/driver-tle92466ed Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-tle92466ed ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE tle92466ed::tle92466ed ) tle92466ed::tle92466ed is an alias of the tle92466ed INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect TLE92466ED_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver TLE92466ED_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-tle92466ed -B build-tle92466ed cmake --install build-tle92466ed --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( tle92466ed 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE tle92466ed::tle92466ed ) The target is tle92466ed::tle92466ed in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated tle92466ed_version.h go to include/tle92466ed/inc/ , the template implementation to include/tle92466ed/src/tle92466ed.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-tle92466ed) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-tle92466ed (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-tle92466ed.git components/tle92466ed tle92466ed (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml tle92466ed (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : tle92466ed : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-tle92466ed.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES tle92466ed (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/tle92466ed_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, sources, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, alias, install rules and the package export, or the ESP-IDF component Tool configuration _config/ Doxyfile, the docs site, Kconfig, clang-format, clang-tidy and the linters Version ¶ The version is set once in the settings file and written into tle92466ed_version.h in the build tree at configure time. The Doxyfile ( _config/Doxyfile ) carries a copy; a host test fails when it differs. Read it at run time: const char * v = tle92466ed :: GetDriverVersion (); // "0.1.0" Next ¶ Quickstart runs the driver on your PC, then on your MCU; Porting writes the port for your MCU.

docs.text: Status and limitations ¶ What this driver has and has not been shown to do, so you can decide whether it is ready for your use. Section numbers refer to the datasheet, Rev. 1.2. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Infineon IFX-ntz1491827137291 1.2: Reset times t_RESN and t_POR: 4.1.3 Electrical characteristics power supply, Table 9, p. 15 Setpoint range and accuracy: 4.6.3 Electrical characteristics current control, Table 14, p. 28 ON-state and OFF-state diagnosis: 4.9.1 TDS_Overview; Figures 14, 15, p. 32 SPI watchdog: 5.2.2 TDS_SPI watchdog; Equation 33, p. 50 Central registers, reset values and bit types: 5.3.1 Overview of Register Types; 5.3.2 Central registers, p. 54 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Status ¶ Version 0.1.0, not released On hardware Not verified on hardware. No board has run this driver yet: run the bench steps below first Tested against A protocol model of the chip written from the datasheet ( Testing and CI ), a fuzzer and the quality gates Assurance level high (Kokeb Labs handbook): not qualified for use in a safety function. The chip is an ASIL C safety element out of context; this driver is not part of any safety case Parts TLE92466ED, design steps A11 (ICVID version 0xFC) and A13 (0xFE). One chip per driver object Interpretations of the datasheet ¶ Where the datasheet leaves room, the driver takes the reading below and a bench step confirms it. Topic The datasheet says The driver Bench step Clearing flags Diagnosis and voltage flags are "cleared on write" (4.1.2, 4.9.1) without a polarity; 5.3.1 defines rwh only as "modifiable by the IC". Counter-evidence: the SFF_BIST result bits clear by writing 0 (4.9.8) Reads every register first and latches it; writes 1 only to the rwh flags that read 1, 0 to the rw ones (POR_EVENT, RES_EVENT, VDD2V5_UV/OV), and nothing to a register with no flag set. Under a write-0 or any-write reading the flags are still read and latched before they go 1, a release gate POR_EVENT Set by any power-on reset; "since the bit was set to 0" (4.1.1) Clears it at start-up, and arms the reset watch only if it then reads 0 2 CHIPID0..2 Drawn with a bits 21..16 row and a six-digit reset value: 22-bit replies (5.3.2.24) Expects 22-bit replies 3 CH_CTRL, MODE, CH_CONFIG rw (5.3.2.3, 5.3.3.10, 5.3.3.11) Writes them whole from its copy and never relies on reading them; Verify::ReadBack reads them 4 SETPOINT rwh (5.3.3.3) Verify::ReadBack compares all 16 bits 4 Read frame bits 23..17 Don't care (5.2.3.2) Sent as 1100000B, so a looped-back frame cannot pass as a reply 5 Reply CRC "Added to all SPI communication frames"; CRC_EN only turns the chip's check off (5.1.2) Checks every reply's CRC, whatever CRC_EN 5 RESN pulse No minimum low time 1 ms ( kResetPulseUs ) 6 INIT_DONE, BIST No duration Polled every 100 µs; INIT_DONE up to Config::init_timeout_us , BIST up to 10 ms 6, 9 Parallel setpoint 2.7 A including dither and overshoot (Table 14, feature list) Refuses a setpoint plus dither amplitude above 2.43 A on a master: the single channel's 1.8 A of its 2.0 A range, the same 90 %, leaves room for the overshoot 7 Critical fault frame Bits 31..24 don't care: no CRC (5.2.3.5) Counts it only when the next frame is one too; then drives EN low and leaves the driver uninitialised 5 VPRE_OV and Mission Mode Figure 4 lists the internal supplies but not VPRE_OV; VPRE_OV does not end Mission Mode (4.1.2) EnterMissionMode() refuses while VPRE_OV is set (SUP_NOK_INT): a fail-safe choice none SPI watchdog at start WD_TIME resets to 1 (0.585 ms) (5.3.2.11) SPI_WD_EN is the last start-up write, after WD_RELOAD; Validate() refuses spi_watchdog with fewer than 9 counts (5.3 ms) 10 Write reply "The actual contents of addressed register will be returned" during the next frame (5.2.1), without saying before or after the write Safe under either reading: the CH_CTRL copy holds an EN_CH or OP_MODE bit only when both the value written and the reply have it, so it can under-report a channel that is on but never report one that is off; every enable change reads CH_CTRL first, the OFF-state overcurrent check counts a channel asked on as on until a read finds it off, and dropped channels are recorded only from a validated read. The host tests run in full under both readings ( tle92466ed_host_tests , tle92466ed_host_tests_reply_before_write ) 4 CH_CTRL after a fault The chip clears EN_CH on a channel fault and leaves Mission Mode on a supply, clock or watchdog fault (4.1.2, 4.2.2, 4.9.2 to 4.9.6, 5.2.2) Reads CH_CTRL before every enable change and after EnterMissionMode() ; never sets an EN_CH bit or OP_MODE it was not asked for 4 A frame the chip ignores "If the number of bits transferred is not 32, the data frame is ignored" (5.1.1) Expects the previous reply to be sent again and refuses a word that repeats in both slots 8 Choices this driver does not make, and why ¶ Each of these is a common shortcut with this chip; the datasheet says otherwise: CRC_EN left on. It is the reset value (5.3.2.4) and protects every configuration write. Turning it off does not help a noisy MISO: the replies carry a CRC either way (5.1.2), and the driver retries a bad read. VIO_SEL at its reset value, 5 V. Forcing 3.3 V on a 5 V board makes VIO read as overvoltage; the board's VIO belongs in Config::vio . Setpoints up to 1.5 A, not 2 A. TARGET reaches 2 A, but values above 0x6000 (1.5 A) are saturated (5.3.3.3) and Table 14 specifies 0 to 1500 mA. The PWM target within 110 Hz to 4 kHz (Table 6), in the low-frequency range too; a target below 110 Hz is refused. WD_TIME is 11 bits (5.3.2.11): at most 2047 counts, 1.198 s at 28 MHz. CHIPID0..2 replies are 22 bits (bench step 3). MIN_INT_THRESH stays at its reset value 0 in Config{} ; the datasheet recommends above 1 (4.6.2.4), and the CurrentControlChannel() preset sets 2. Bench steps ¶ Run these on a board with a TLE92466ED, VDD at 5 V, VBAT at 12 V to 14 V and a solenoid or a 10 Ω, 1 mH load on LOAD0 with its freewheeling diode, using the ESP32 example or your own port. Record each result in the pull request. Flag clearing. A release gate: no final (non-rc) release before this step has passed. Inject a VBAT undervoltage (lower VBAT below 4 V, then restore it). ReadFaults() shows VbatUndervoltage ; ClearFaults() ; ReadFaults() shows it clear. Set OLSG on CH0 (disconnect the load, enable at 100 mA) and on CH1; ClearChannelFaults(Ch0) clears CH0's flag and leaves CH1's set, so a write to one channel's byte does not clear the other's. With every flag clear, ReadRegister() of DIAG_ERR_CHGR0 after writing 0x1F1F to it (a debugger or a test build) still reads 0: writing 1 to a clear flag does not set it. Also check that POR_EVENT clears with a 0, and that OC needs exactly two clears. POR_EVENT. After EnsureInitialized() , IsResetWatchArmed() is true. Pulse VDD off for 100 ms: the next ReloadWatchdog() or SetCurrent() returns UnexpectedReset . CHIPID width. ReadChipId() returns Ok and the same ID on every call. Read-back and the write reply. Find which reading the chip uses: write CH_CTRL with CH_PAR_4_5 set in Config Mode, then again with it clear, and capture the second write's reply on a logic analyser (CH_PAR_4_5 set: the reply is the contents before the write; clear: after). The driver is safe under either; the answer only says how often the copy under-reports. With OL latched on CH0, EnableChannel(Ch0) without read-back leaves GetEnabledChannels() at 0 and GetDroppedChannels() at 0; the next ReadChannelControl() shows CH0 in GetDroppedChannels() . EnterMissionMode() , EnableChannel(Ch0, Verify::ReadBack) , SetCurrent(Ch0, 300000, Verify::ReadBack) and ConfigureChannel(..., Verify::ReadBack) in Config Mode all return Ok . Frames. At 1 MHz and at 8 MHz, ReadRegister(0x0200) returns 0xC1FC or 0xC1FE; GetBusDiagnostics() shows no rejected reply over 10000 calls. Capture one access on a logic analyser: the request, the anchor, CSN high at least 600 ns between them. Reset and readiness. Scope RESN and SO through EnsureInitialized() : RESN low for 1 ms, the first FB_STAT reads INIT_DONE = 1 within a few polls. Repeat with RESN tied high (a port without GpioSet() ). Current. In Mission Mode, set CH0 to 100 mA, 500 mA and 1000 mA: ReadChannelFeedback() reports within ±2.5 mA below 250 mA and ±1 % above (Table 14), and a clamp meter agrees. Join CH1 and CH2, load them with one coil, set 2 A: the feedback reports the sum. Ignored frame. With a logic analyser that can inject, cut one request frame short (31 clocks): the call returns ReplyMismatch (a write) or succeeds after one retry (a read). Self-test. RunBist() in Config Mode returns passed , both error classes tested, within 10 ms; afterwards EnterMissionMode() works. SPI watchdog. With spi_watchdog and a 50 ms timeout, stop calling ReloadWatchdog() : every channel turns off within 50 ms, ReadStatus() shows spi_watchdog_error , and a reload plus ClearFaults() lets EnterMissionMode() work again. Diagnosis. Open the load of CH0 while it regulates 300 mA with ol_fixed = 6: OLSG sets and the channel turns off; with the setpoint kept and EN_CH off, the OFF-state diagnosis reports OL. Short LOAD0 to ground: it reports SG. Short LOAD0 to VBAT and run StartOvercurrentCheck(Ch0) with on_time_mant = 100: OC sets. ESP32 port timing. Scope CSN and SCK at 2 MHz: t_CSN_LEAD and t_CSN_LAG at least 250 ns. Not covered ¶ Supply-monitor and overtemperature test modes (GLOBAL_CONFIG.UV_OV_SWAP, OT_TEST, V1V5_UV/OV_TEST): the last two reset the chip on purpose. Use them only with a custom sequence. FB_I_AVG_s16 and FB_INT_THRESH have no decoded call; ReadRegister() reads them. Daisy chains and more than one chip per driver object.

docs.text: Where the datasheet leaves room, the driver takes the reading below and a bench step confirms it. Topic The datasheet says The driver Bench step Clearing flags Diagnosis and voltage flags are "cleared on write" (4.1.2, 4.9.1) without a polarity; 5.3.1 defines rwh only as "modifiable by the IC". Counter-evidence: the SFF_BIST result bits clear by writing 0 (4.9.8) Reads every register first and latches it; writes 1 only to the rwh flags that read 1, 0 to the rw ones (POR_EVENT, RES_EVENT, VDD2V5_UV/OV), and nothing to a register with no flag set. Under a write-0 or any-write reading the flags are still read and latched before they go 1, a release gate POR_EVENT Set by any power-on reset; "since the bit was set to 0" (4.1.1) Clears it at start-up, and arms the reset watch only if it then reads 0 2 CHIPID0..2 Drawn with a bits 21..16 row and a six-digit reset value: 22-bit replies (5.3.2.24) Expects 22-bit replies 3 CH_CTRL, MODE, CH_CONFIG rw (5.3.2.3, 5.3.3.10, 5.3.3.11) Writes them whole from its copy and never relies on reading them; Verify::ReadBack reads them 4 SETPOINT rwh (5.3.3.3) Verify::ReadBack compares all 16 bits 4 Read frame bits 23..17 Don't care (5.2.3.2) Sent as 1100000B, so a looped-back frame cannot pass as a reply 5 Reply CRC "Added to all SPI communication frames"; CRC_EN only turns the chip's check off (5.1.2) Checks every reply's CRC, whatever CRC_EN 5 RESN pulse No minimum low time 1 ms ( kResetPulseUs ) 6 INIT_DONE, BIST No duration Polled every 100 µs; INIT_DONE up to Config::init_timeout_us , BIST up to 10 ms 6, 9 Parallel setpoint 2.7 A including dither and overshoot (Table 14, feature list) Refuses a setpoint plus dither amplitude above 2.43 A on a master: the single channel's 1.8 A of its 2.0 A range, the same 90 %, leaves room for the overshoot 7 Critical fault frame Bits 31..24 don't care: no CRC (5.2.3.5) Counts it only when the next frame is one too; then drives EN low and leaves the driver uninitialised 5 VPRE_OV and Mission Mode Figure 4 lists the internal supplies but not VPRE_OV; VPRE_OV does not end Mission Mode (4.1.2) EnterMissionMode() refuses while VPRE_OV is set (SUP_NOK_INT): a fail-safe choice none SPI watchdog at start WD_TIME resets to 1 (0.585 ms) (5.3.2.11) SPI_WD_EN is the last start-up write, after WD_RELOAD; Validate() refuses spi_watchdog with fewer than 9 counts (5.3 ms) 10 Write reply "The actual contents of addressed register will be returned" during the next frame (5.2.1), without saying before or after the write Safe under either reading: the CH_CTRL copy holds an EN_CH or OP_MODE bit only when both the value written and the reply have it, so it can under-report a channel that is on but never report one that is off; every enable change reads CH_CTRL first, the OFF-state overcurrent check counts a channel asked on as on until a read finds it off, and dropped channels are recorded only from a validated read. The host tests run in full under both readings ( tle92466ed_host_tests , tle92466ed_host_tests_reply_before_write ) 4 CH_CTRL after a fault The chip clears EN_CH on a channel fault and leaves Mission Mode on a supply, clock or watchdog fault (4.1.2, 4.2.2, 4.9.2 to 4.9.6, 5.2.2) Reads CH_CTRL before every enable change and after EnterMissionMode() ; never sets an EN_CH bit or OP_MODE it was not asked for 4 A frame the chip ignores "If the number of bits transferred is not 32, the data frame is ignored" (5.1.1) Expects the previous reply to be sent again and refuses a word that repeats in both slots 8

docs.text: Each of these is a common shortcut with this chip; the datasheet says otherwise: CRC_EN left on. It is the reset value (5.3.2.4) and protects every configuration write. Turning it off does not help a noisy MISO: the replies carry a CRC either way (5.1.2), and the driver retries a bad read. VIO_SEL at its reset value, 5 V. Forcing 3.3 V on a 5 V board makes VIO read as overvoltage; the board's VIO belongs in Config::vio . Setpoints up to 1.5 A, not 2 A. TARGET reaches 2 A, but values above 0x6000 (1.5 A) are saturated (5.3.3.3) and Table 14 specifies 0 to 1500 mA. The PWM target within 110 Hz to 4 kHz (Table 6), in the low-frequency range too; a target below 110 Hz is refused. WD_TIME is 11 bits (5.3.2.11): at most 2047 counts, 1.198 s at 28 MHz. CHIPID0..2 replies are 22 bits (bench step 3). MIN_INT_THRESH stays at its reset value 0 in Config{} ; the datasheet recommends above 1 (4.6.2.4), and the CurrentControlChannel() preset sets 2.

docs.text: Run these on a board with a TLE92466ED, VDD at 5 V, VBAT at 12 V to 14 V and a solenoid or a 10 Ω, 1 mH load on LOAD0 with its freewheeling diode, using the ESP32 example or your own port. Record each result in the pull request. Flag clearing. A release gate: no final (non-rc) release before this step has passed. Inject a VBAT undervoltage (lower VBAT below 4 V, then restore it). ReadFaults() shows VbatUndervoltage ; ClearFaults() ; ReadFaults() shows it clear. Set OLSG on CH0 (disconnect the load, enable at 100 mA) and on CH1; ClearChannelFaults(Ch0) clears CH0's flag and leaves CH1's set, so a write to one channel's byte does not clear the other's. With every flag clear, ReadRegister() of DIAG_ERR_CHGR0 after writing 0x1F1F to it (a debugger or a test build) still reads 0: writing 1 to a clear flag does not set it. Also check that POR_EVENT clears with a 0, and that OC needs exactly two clears. POR_EVENT. After EnsureInitialized() , IsResetWatchArmed() is true. Pulse VDD off for 100 ms: the next ReloadWatchdog() or SetCurrent() returns UnexpectedReset . CHIPID width. ReadChipId() returns Ok and the same ID on every call. Read-back and the write reply. Find which reading the chip uses: write CH_CTRL with CH_PAR_4_5 set in Config Mode, then again with it clear, and capture the second write's reply on a logic analyser (CH_PAR_4_5 set: the reply is the contents before the write; clear: after). The driver is safe under either; the answer only says how often the copy under-reports. With OL latched on CH0, EnableChannel(Ch0) without read-back leaves GetEnabledChannels() at 0 and GetDroppedChannels() at 0; the next ReadChannelControl() shows CH0 in GetDroppedChannels() . EnterMissionMode() , EnableChannel(Ch0, Verify::ReadBack) , SetCurrent(Ch0, 300000, Verify::ReadBack) and ConfigureChannel(..., Verify::ReadBack) in Config Mode all return Ok . Frames. At 1 MHz and at 8 MHz, ReadRegister(0x0200) returns 0xC1FC or 0xC1FE; GetBusDiagnostics() shows no rejected reply over 10000 calls. Capture one access on a logic analyser: the request, the anchor, CSN high at least 600 ns between them. Reset and readiness. Scope RESN and SO through EnsureInitialized() : RESN low for 1 ms, the first FB_STAT reads INIT_DONE = 1 within a few polls. Repeat with RESN tied high (a port without GpioSet() ). Current. In Mission Mode, set CH0 to 100 mA, 500 mA and 1000 mA: ReadChannelFeedback() reports within ±2.5 mA below 250 mA and ±1 % above (Table 14), and a clamp meter agrees. Join CH1 and CH2, load them with one coil, set 2 A: the feedback reports the sum. Ignored frame. With a logic analyser that can inject, cut one request frame short (31 clocks): the call returns ReplyMismatch (a write) or succeeds after one retry (a read). Self-test. RunBist() in Config Mode returns passed , both error classes tested, within 10 ms; afterwards EnterMissionMode() works. SPI watchdog. With spi_watchdog and a 50 ms timeout, stop calling ReloadWatchdog() : every channel turns off within 50 ms, ReadStatus() shows spi_watchdog_error , and a reload plus ClearFaults() lets EnterMissionMode() work again. Diagnosis. Open the load of CH0 while it regulates 300 mA with ol_fixed = 6: OLSG sets and the channel turns off; with the setpoint kept and EN_CH off, the OFF-state diagnosis reports OL. Short LOAD0 to ground: it reports SG. Short LOAD0 to VBAT and run StartOvercurrentCheck(Ch0) with on_time_mant = 100: OC sets. ESP32 port timing. Scope CSN and SCK at 2 MHz: t_CSN_LEAD and t_CSN_LAG at least 250 ns.

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the port. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Infineon IFX-ntz1491827137291 1.2: Pins, RESN, EN, DRV0/DRV1 and FAULTN: 2 Pin configuration; 4.2.3 TDS_I/O Pins, p. 7 SPI frame, mode and CRC-8 SAE J1850: 5.1.1 TDS_General information; 5.1.2 TDS_Cyclic redundancy check (CRC), p. 47 SPI timing: 5.1.4 Electrical characteristics SPI interface, Table 18, p. 48 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver never calls your SDK. It calls hooks on a class you derive from tle92466ed::SpiInterface<Self> (in inc/tle92466ed_spi_interface.hpp ). The base uses CRTP and declares no hook itself; the driver template is constrained by the tle92466ed::SpiPort concept, so calls are resolved at compile time (no virtual functions, nothing to allocate) and a missing or misdeclared hook is a compile error at the point of use. What you implement ¶ Method Required Contract bool EnsureInitialized() noexcept yes Bring the bus up on the first call; return true at once afterwards. false makes the driver's EnsureInitialized() return Bus bool Transfer(const uint8_t* tx, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t len) noexcept yes One full-duplex 32-bit frame: len is always 4, both buffers are given, CSN low for the 4 bytes and high after. false on any bus error void DelayUs(uint32_t us) noexcept yes, for every wait Wait at least us microseconds bool GpioSet(CtrlPin, GpioSignal) noexcept no Drive RESN, EN, DRV0 or DRV1; false if the pin write failed; true for a pin tied on the board bool GpioRead(CtrlPin, GpioSignal&) noexcept no Read FAULTN ( CtrlPin::Fault ); false if it cannot be read void Log(LogLevel, const char* message) noexcept no Print one line; message is plain text, never a format string The port ¶ my_port.hpp class MyPort : public tle92466ed :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One 32-bit frame: CSN low for the 4 bytes, both buffers given, CSN high after. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: t_POR and the INIT_DONE polls depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Rules the transfer must follow: One call, one frame. Keep CSN low for the 4 bytes; the chip takes the frame only when exactly 32 bits were clocked between the CSN edges (section 5.1.1). Raise CSN after it for at least 600 ns. The bus requirements below : mode 1, MSB first, up to kMaxClockHz . Start at 2 MHz on jumper wires. Raw bytes only. Do not interpret, retry or reorder bytes; the driver owns the framing, the CRC and the retries. Return false for a bus error. The driver turns it into Error::Bus and never ignores it. Bounded time-outs. A stuck bus fails the call; it does not block forever. No other frames to this chip during a call. A call's frames belong together: the reply to each comes in the next. Hold your bus lock for the whole driver call when tasks share the driver; other devices on the bus may use it between the frames, since this chip ignores SCK while its CSN is high. Buffers the bus can reach. The driver's frame buffers are members of the driver object; if your SPI uses DMA from a restricted memory region, place the driver object there. Bus requirements ¶ The driver states what the TLE92466ED needs from the bus as constexpr values in inc/tle92466ed_spi_interface.hpp (handbook KB-CPP-123). Check your port's settings against them with static_assert , as both example ports do, so a port that clocks too fast or in the wrong mode does not compile: Constant Value Meaning (datasheet 5.1, Table 18) kSpiMode 1 CPOL 0, CPHA 1: SO changes on the rising edge, SI is sampled on the falling edge kMsbFirst true Most significant bit first kMaxClockHz 8'000'000 f_SCK max kMinCsHighNs 600 CSN high between two frames, t_CSN_TD kCsSetupNs , kCsHoldNs 250 , 250 CSN low to the first SCK edge (t_CSN_LEAD), last SCK edge to CSN high (t_CSN_LAG) kContinuousWord false Idle SCK time inside a frame is allowed; the chip counts 32 clocks kFrameBytes 4 One 32-bit frame per transfer Control pins ¶ Each control pin has a defined idle level, and the port drives it there before it enables the pin's output and before the driver's first transfer (handbook KB-HW-018). Configuring a pin as an output first and setting its level afterwards gives the chip a pulse it did not ask for, for example a reset. CtrlPin Package pin Polarity Idle level Before the first transfer Reset RESN (26) active low low, ACTIVE : in reset Set low, then enable the output Enable EN (27) active high low, INACTIVE Set low, then enable the output Drv0 , Drv1 DRV0 (25), DRV1 (28) active high low, INACTIVE Set low, then enable the output Fault FAULTN (11) active low, open drain input with a pull-up to VIO Configure as an input GpioSignal::ACTIVE always means "function asserted"; the port maps it to the electrical level. RESN idles in reset so the chip, and every output, stays off from the MCU's reset until EnsureInitialized() releases it. A pin tied on the board needs no hook, or a hook that returns true for it. Optional hooks ¶ The driver finds the optional hooks at compile time with C++20 requires , in one place ( tle92466ed::detail ). A missing hook falls back in a documented, safe way or fails to compile; it never skips a step silently. Hook Used for Without it DelayUs() t_POR or t_RESN at start-up, the INIT_DONE and self-test polls Compile error at the first call that waits GpioSet() RESN pulse in EnsureInitialized() and HardwareReset() ; EN in EnterMissionMode() , EnterConfigMode() , Deinitialize() ; SetDrivePin() EnsureInitialized() waits t_POR; HardwareReset() and SetDrivePin() return Error::Unsupported GpioRead() ReadFaultPin() ReadFaultPin() returns Error::Unsupported Log() One line per lifecycle event or start-up failure Nothing is logged A port with every hook: class FullPort : public tle92466ed :: SpiInterface < FullPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { // Before the bus: RESN low (in reset), EN, DRV0 and DRV1 low (handbook KB-HW-018). return platform_gpio_write ( kResn , false ) && platform_gpio_write ( kEn , false ) && platform_gpio_write ( kDrv0 , false ) && platform_gpio_write ( kDrv1 , false ) && platform_spi_init (); } bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Required by every call that waits (reset, INIT_DONE, self-test). void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: RESN, EN, DRV0, DRV1. ACTIVE on RESN means "in reset", a low level on the pin. bool GpioSet ( tle92466ed :: CtrlPin pin , tle92466ed :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { const bool active = signal == tle92466ed :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ; switch ( pin ) { case tle92466ed :: CtrlPin :: Reset : return platform_gpio_write ( kResn , ! active ); case tle92466ed :: CtrlPin :: Enable : return platform_gpio_write ( kEn , active ); case tle92466ed :: CtrlPin :: Drv0 : return platform_gpio_write ( kDrv0 , active ); case tle92466ed :: CtrlPin :: Drv1 : return platform_gpio_write ( kDrv1 , active ); default : return false ; // FAULTN is an input } } // Optional: FAULTN, open drain with a pull-up. ACTIVE (a fault) is a low level. bool GpioRead ( tle92466ed :: CtrlPin pin , tle92466ed :: GpioSignal & signal ) noexcept { bool high = true ; if (( pin != tle92466ed :: CtrlPin :: Fault ) || ! platform_gpio_read ( kFaultn , high )) { return false ; } signal = high ? tle92466ed :: GpioSignal :: INACTIVE : tle92466ed :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ; return true ; } // Optional: one line per lifecycle event or failure. The driver never formats; the port does. void Log ( tle92466ed :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { if ( level > tle92466ed :: LogLevel :: Warning ) { return ; } platform_log ( message ); // plain text: never use it as a format string } private : static constexpr int kResn = 7 ; static constexpr int kEn = 8 ; static constexpr int kDrv0 = 9 ; static constexpr int kDrv1 = 10 ; static constexpr int kFaultn = 11 ; }; tle92466ed :: Error RecoverFromCriticalFault ( tle92466ed :: TLE92466ED < FullPort >& driver ) { // Only RESN or a power cycle leaves the Critical Fault state; without GpioSet() this call // returns Error::Unsupported. return driver . HardwareReset (). error ; } A GpioSet() that returns void , or a GpioRead() that takes the level by value, is a compile error: the driver must see a failed pin write and must get the level back. The compile-fail tests check these rules. Reference implementations ¶ Every port lives with its example, in examples/<platform>/ ; the driver has none. Platforms lists them and how to add one. examples/host/host_tle92466ed_port.hpp : any PC, against a simulated chip. Start from it for a host build or a test bench; it is also the smallest complete port. examples/esp32/main/esp32_tle92466ed_port.hpp : ESP-IDF, with every hook. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the ports on this page are compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over them. Call EnsureInitialized() : Ok proves that frames go both ways with valid CRCs, that ICVID read 0xC1 and that GLOBAL_CONFIG read back what was written. Call ReadSupply() : VIO and VDD read within a few percent of your meter; GetBusDiagnostics().retries stays 0. With a load on LOAD0, EnterMissionMode() , SetCurrent() , EnableChannel() , then ReadChannelFeedback() : the average current is within 1 % (2.5 mA below 250 mA) of the setpoint. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each driver object one owner task, or guard every call with one mutex. When several devices share a bus, the port must also serialise the bus. See Contract . Editor setup ¶ The clang-format and clang-tidy configuration is in _config/ , and the repository root has no copy of it. Tools that take a path use it directly; CI does the same: Tool Setting Command line clang-format --style=file:_config/.clang-format , clang-tidy --config-file=_config/.clang-tidy -p build VS Code (C/C++ extension) "C_Cpp.clang_format_style": "file:${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-format" and "C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.args": ["--config-file=${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-tidy"] clangd (VS Code clangd, Neovim, Emacs), CLion These find .clang-format and .clang-tidy only by name, from the file upwards: copy both to the root once ( cp _config/.clang-format _config/.clang-tidy . ). .gitignore lists the copies, so they never reach a commit; copy again after _config/ changes Configure with -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON (clangd: --compile-commands-dir=build ) so the editor sees the same flags as the build.

Buffers the bus can reach. The driver's frame buffers are members of the driver object; if your SPI uses DMA from a restricted memory region, place the driver object there.

docs.text: Each control pin has a defined idle level, and the port drives it there before it enables the pin's output and before the driver's first transfer (handbook KB-HW-018). Configuring a pin as an output first and setting its level afterwards gives the chip a pulse it did not ask for, for example a reset. CtrlPin Package pin Polarity Idle level Before the first transfer Reset RESN (26) active low low, ACTIVE : in reset Set low, then enable the output Enable EN (27) active high low, INACTIVE Set low, then enable the output Drv0 , Drv1 DRV0 (25), DRV1 (28) active high low, INACTIVE Set low, then enable the output Fault FAULTN (11) active low, open drain input with a pull-up to VIO Configure as an input GpioSignal::ACTIVE always means "function asserted"; the port maps it to the electrical level. RESN idles in reset so the chip, and every output, stays off from the MCU's reset until EnsureInitialized() releases it. A pin tied on the board needs no hook, or a hook that returns true for it.

docs.text: The driver finds the optional hooks at compile time with C++20 requires , in one place ( tle92466ed::detail ). A missing hook falls back in a documented, safe way or fails to compile; it never skips a step silently. Hook Used for Without it DelayUs() t_POR or t_RESN at start-up, the INIT_DONE and self-test polls Compile error at the first call that waits GpioSet() RESN pulse in EnsureInitialized() and HardwareReset() ; EN in EnterMissionMode() , EnterConfigMode() , Deinitialize() ; SetDrivePin() EnsureInitialized() waits t_POR; HardwareReset() and SetDrivePin() return Error::Unsupported GpioRead() ReadFaultPin() ReadFaultPin() returns Error::Unsupported Log() One line per lifecycle event or start-up failure Nothing is logged A port with every hook: class FullPort : public tle92466ed :: SpiInterface < FullPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { // Before the bus: RESN low (in reset), EN, DRV0 and DRV1 low (handbook KB-HW-018). return platform_gpio_write ( kResn , false ) && platform_gpio_write ( kEn , false ) && platform_gpio_write ( kDrv0 , false ) && platform_gpio_write ( kDrv1 , false ) && platform_spi_init (); } bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Required by every call that waits (reset, INIT_DONE, self-test). void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: RESN, EN, DRV0, DRV1. ACTIVE on RESN means "in reset", a low level on the pin. bool GpioSet ( tle92466ed :: CtrlPin pin , tle92466ed :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { const bool active = signal == tle92466ed :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ; switch ( pin ) { case tle92466ed :: CtrlPin :: Reset : return platform_gpio_write ( kResn , ! active ); case tle92466ed :: CtrlPin :: Enable : return platform_gpio_write ( kEn , active ); case tle92466ed :: CtrlPin :: Drv0 : return platform_gpio_write ( kDrv0 , active ); case tle92466ed :: CtrlPin :: Drv1 : return platform_gpio_write ( kDrv1 , active ); default : return false ; // FAULTN is an input } } // Optional: FAULTN, open drain with a pull-up. ACTIVE (a fault) is a low level. bool GpioRead ( tle92466ed :: CtrlPin pin , tle92466ed :: GpioSignal & signal ) noexcept { bool high = true ; if (( pin != tle92466ed :: CtrlPin :: Fault ) || ! platform_gpio_read ( kFaultn , high )) { return false ; } signal = high ? tle92466ed :: GpioSignal :: INACTIVE : tle92466ed :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ; return true ; } // Optional: one line per lifecycle event or failure. The driver never formats; the port does. void Log ( tle92466ed :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { if ( level > tle92466ed :: LogLevel :: Warning ) { return ; } platform_log ( message ); // plain text: never use it as a format string } private : static constexpr int kResn = 7 ; static constexpr int kEn = 8 ; static constexpr int kDrv0 = 9 ; static constexpr int kDrv1 = 10 ; static constexpr int kFaultn = 11 ; }; tle92466ed :: Error RecoverFromCriticalFault ( tle92466ed :: TLE92466ED < FullPort >& driver ) { // Only RESN or a power cycle leaves the Critical Fault state; without GpioSet() this call // returns Error::Unsupported. return driver . HardwareReset (). error ; } A GpioSet() that returns void , or a GpioRead() that takes the level by value, is a compile error: the driver must see a failed pin write and must get the level back. The compile-fail tests check these rules.

Datasheet sections this page relies on From Infineon IFX-ntz1491827137291 1.2: Pins, RESN, EN, DRV0/DRV1 and FAULTN: 2 Pin configuration; 4.2.3 TDS_I/O Pins, p. 7 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Try it on your PC ¶ examples/host/ runs the real driver against a simulated TLE92466ED, through a host port. From the repository root, with CMake and a C++20 compiler: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example cmake --build build-example ./build-example/tle92466ed_host_example TLE92466ED driver 0.1.0 on the host tle92466ed: initialised, Config Mode ICVID version 0xFE, reset watch armed CH0 setpoint 399976 uA CH0 397714 uA, duty 40.00 %, VBAT 13981 mV The calls in main.cpp are the ones below; only the port differs on an MCU. CI builds and runs this example on every pull request. 1. Wire it ¶ MCU TLE92466ED Notes SPI SCK SCK (6) Mode 1, up to 8 MHz; 2 MHz for bring-up on jumper wires SPI MOSI SI (7) SPI MISO SO (9) Driven from VIO; high impedance while CSN is high GPIO (chip select) CSN (5) Low for one 32-bit frame, then high for at least 600 ns MCU supply VIO (8) 3.3 V or 5 V: set Config::vio to match 5 V VDD (29) 4.5 V to 5.5 V, 100 nF to GND Load supply VBAT (22) 6 V to 18 V; the valve between VBAT and LOAD0, a freewheeling diode to FWD0 GND GND, GNDP0..5, tab All grounds together For this example tie RESN (26) and EN (27) to VIO through 10 kΩ, DRV0 and DRV1 to GND, and leave FAULTN open: a port without GpioSet() then starts the chip by waiting t_POR. The Hardware page has every pin, the timing and the application circuit. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the tle92466ed::tle92466ed CMake target. Installation covers CMake on any MCU, the installed package and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-tle92466ed.git external/driver-tle92466ed 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code: it brings the bus up and moves 32-bit frames. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_port.hpp class MyPort : public tle92466ed :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One 32-bit frame: CSN low for the 4 bytes, both buffers given, CSN high after. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: t_POR and the INIT_DONE polls depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Porting explains each method, the optional hooks and the transfer rules. 4. Drive a valve ¶ main.cpp #include "tle92466ed.hpp" int drive_one_valve ( MyPort & port ) { tle92466ed :: Config config {}; // reset values, no channel loaded config . vio = tle92466ed :: VioLevel :: V3V3 ; // the board's VIO config . channels [ 0 ] = tle92466ed :: CurrentControlChannel (); // CH0: a valve, ICC, 1 kHz PWM tle92466ed :: TLE92466ED < MyPort > driver ( port , config ); // no I/O yet if ( auto r = driver . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 1. reset, INIT_DONE, ICVID, every register return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // Bus, NoDevice, Timeout: check the wiring } if ( auto r = driver . EnterMissionMode (); ! r ) { // 2. EN high, OP_MODE = 1 return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // MissionBlocked: read the faults } if ( auto r = driver . SetCurrent ( tle92466ed :: Channel :: Ch0 , 400'000 ); ! r ) { // 3. 400 mA return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); } return static_cast < int > ( driver . EnableChannel ( tle92466ed :: Channel :: Ch0 ). error ); // 4. on } What each step does: EnsureInitialized() brings the port up, resets or waits out the chip, waits for INIT_DONE, checks ICVID, reports and clears the faults found, and writes every register. The chip is in Config Mode, every channel off. EnterMissionMode() checks that no supply, clock or watchdog fault holds the chip in Config Mode, then sets OP_MODE. Only in Mission Mode do the channels switch and their diagnosis run. SetCurrent() programs the average current; the value is checked against 1.5 A, rounded to the 61 µA TARGET step, and the programmed current is returned. EnableChannel() sets EN_CH0: the integrating current controller now holds 400 mA through the valve. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check EnsureInitialized() returns Bus Your port's EnsureInitialized() or Transfer() returned false EnsureInitialized() returns NoDevice VIO, SO and CSN: MISO reads all zeros or all ones ( Troubleshooting ) EnsureInitialized() returns Crc or ReplyMismatch The SPI mode (it must be 1) and the clock EnsureInitialized() returns Timeout VDD and RESN: INIT_DONE never read 1 EnterMissionMode() returns MissionBlocked Config::vio against the real VIO, then ReadFaults() ReadChannelFeedback() returns NotReady The channel's dither clock: no measurement period without one Next ¶ API guide : states, channels, feedback, faults, the watchdog, errors. Configuration : the current-control preset, every Config field, Kconfig. Examples : the host example and the ESP32 example. Status and limitations : what still needs a bench.

Each one is a dry run unless given --apply , and --repo limits it to one repository. The rules behind them are in repo-governance.md . 1. Create and scaffold ¶ gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --public --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in. 2. Apply the org settings ¶ From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR. Its entry sets the About: the description is the README's first sentence ( C++20 driver for the <vendor> <parts> <what it is> (<bus>) ), and the topics are the shared kokeb-labs driver embedded cpp20 misra-cpp header-only plus the bus, the device category, the vendor and the part ( spi eeprom microchip at25040b ): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --repo driver-<chip> # the plan: every setting that would change python3 org/kokeb_org.py --repo driver-<chip> --apply # settings, security, Actions, rulesets, labels A private repository on the free plan gets the settings, Actions policy and labels; security features and rulesets need it public (the tool says which sections it skips).
