docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against a model of the chip, a fuzzer that corrupts what the chip sends back, compiled documentation, an install test, ESP32 and Cortex-M builds, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request. Host tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a protocol and register model of the TLE92466ED: 32-bit frames with the CRC it checks while CRC_EN is set, the reply one frame later in the 16-bit, 22-bit or critical fault format, the reset values, Config and Mission Mode with their rules, clear-on-write flags with the two clears OC and OTP_ECC_ERR need, a channel kept off while it has a fault, parallel pairs, INIT_DONE, the SPI watchdog, the feedback freeze with a measurement period from the dither clock, and the self-test. The mock bus adds the faults a real line shows: a failed transfer, MISO stuck low or high, MOSI looped back, a bit flipped on MISO or MOSI, a frame the chip ignores or never sees, a reply replaced by any word. They build with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. cmake -S . -B build -DTLE92466ED_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_tle92466ed.cpp Start-up (each step and each failure), the calls before the start, operation states, the SPI watchdog, configuration, reset detection tests/test_channels.cpp Enables, setpoints and their limits, parallel pairs, dither, the OFF-state overcurrent check, the DRV pins tests/test_diagnostics.cpp Status, faults and the latch, clearing, feedback, supplies, pins, self-test, chip ID, the raw read tests/test_protocol.cpp The frame layout and CRC, the bus requirements, stuck and looped-back lines, retries, never-retried writes, ignored and lost frames, the anchor, the status field, critical fault frames, resynchronisation tests/test_state_safety.cpp The driver's copy never overrides the chip: faulted channels stay off, Mission Mode only as Figure 4 allows, flags read before they are cleared, critical faults and resets turn EN off, the start-up order, the frame counts tests/test_ambiguous_writes.cpp A write whose reply failed or whose frame was lost: every guard that depends on what it may have changed refuses with WrongState and no frame, until a read or a successful write (setpoint, EN_CH, OP_MODE, pairs, channel, dither and global registers) tests/test_bus_faults.cpp Every transfer of every operation failing in turn is Error::Bus tests/test_types.cpp Validate() against every documented range, the conversions and decoders at run time tests/fuzz/ The fuzz target; The model's limits ¶ The model is written from the datasheet, so it shares the driver's reading of the datasheet wherever the datasheet leaves room. These shared assumptions are not proven by the tests; each has a bench step in Status and limitations : A 1 clears an rwh flag and a 0 leaves it; an rw flag takes the value written; OC and OTP_ECC_ERR need two clears. CH_CTRL, MODE, CH_CONFIG and SETPOINT read back what was written; a slave reads MODE and SETPOINT as 0. The reply to a write carries the register after the write. Section 5.2.1 allows the contents before it too, so the knob write_reply_before_write gives that reading and tle92466ed_host_tests_reply_before_write runs every host test under it (the build defines TLE92466ED_MODEL_REPLY_BEFORE_WRITE ); the driver must pass both. CHIPID0..2 and every register from FB_STAT on answer with 22-bit replies. A frame the chip ignores leaves the previous reply to be sent again; the first reply after a reset is all zeros. The don't-care bits of a read frame are ignored; replies always carry a CRC. INIT_DONE after a reset or a clock change takes init_delay_us (50 µs), the self-test 500 µs: the datasheet gives neither. The feedback is synthetic (the setpoint, or load_ua , over one dither period); the frame time is 32 SCK periods plus 1 µs at 4 MHz. An OC in a pair disables both channels; COTERR switches every stage off and keeps Mission Mode; VPRE_OV switches them off; COTWARN and VBAT faults are reported only; a channel OTW or OTE blocks Mission Mode entry. CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request, from the seeds plus a corpus it keeps between runs (job Host quality / fuzz ). Quality gates ¶ The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target no broken promise The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DTLE92466ED_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DTLE92466ED_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( tle92466ed_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/tle92466ed.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published. Documentation snippets ¶ Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target tle92466ed_doc_snippets ) with the driver instantiated over the documented port. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. The README's example is a generated copy of the same file; kokeb-docs check fails when it drifts. CI workflows ¶ Everything runs from ci.yml , which calls one workflow file per check and ends in the CI gate job, the single required check ( CI gate / gate ). Job What it checks Host tests GCC, then Clang (one job), build and run every test above, then build and run examples/host on its own Host quality The gates above: complexity, coverage, sanitizers, fuzzing Cross-compile arm-none-eabi-g++ for Cortex-M0+, M4F and M7F with the strict flags, warnings as errors (nothing linked) C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy over the sources MISRA MISRA C++:2023 and the C++20 profile on traced host and Cortex-M builds, at level high (see Quality gates ) Docs Strict site build ( _config/mkdocs.yml ), figure and generated-region drift, Doxygen ( _config/Doxyfile ), offline link check, Lighthouse Repository checks One job: DCO on pull requests, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the Kokeb Labs handbook rules for .kokeb/handbook.yml (by rule ID), template drift (warns only) and cppcheck over the driver sources; a second job runs the handbook's source checks (include guards, bus requirements, raw access) CI gate Passes only if every job above passed: the one required check The ESP32 examples job builds every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type, with the repository root as the driver's component, and lints the example sources. The gate needs it too. The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of kokeb-labs/ci-tools at @v1 . On hardware ¶ The ESP32 example ( Examples ) is the bench test: it drives LOAD0 at 300 mA and logs its feedback and any fault twice a second. The bench steps, and what each confirms, are in Status and limitations . Record the board and the result in the pull request's bench-status section.

docs.text: The model is written from the datasheet, so it shares the driver's reading of the datasheet wherever the datasheet leaves room. These shared assumptions are not proven by the tests; each has a bench step in Status and limitations : A 1 clears an rwh flag and a 0 leaves it; an rw flag takes the value written; OC and OTP_ECC_ERR need two clears. CH_CTRL, MODE, CH_CONFIG and SETPOINT read back what was written; a slave reads MODE and SETPOINT as 0. The reply to a write carries the register after the write. Section 5.2.1 allows the contents before it too, so the knob write_reply_before_write gives that reading and tle92466ed_host_tests_reply_before_write runs every host test under it (the build defines TLE92466ED_MODEL_REPLY_BEFORE_WRITE ); the driver must pass both. CHIPID0..2 and every register from FB_STAT on answer with 22-bit replies. A frame the chip ignores leaves the previous reply to be sent again; the first reply after a reset is all zeros. The don't-care bits of a read frame are ignored; replies always carry a CRC. INIT_DONE after a reset or a clock change takes init_delay_us (50 µs), the self-test 500 µs: the datasheet gives neither. The feedback is synthetic (the setpoint, or load_ua , over one dither period); the frame time is 32 SCK periods plus 1 µs at 4 MHz. An OC in a pair disables both channels; COTERR switches every stage off and keeps Mission Mode; VPRE_OV switches them off; COTWARN and VBAT faults are reported only; a channel OTW or OTE blocks Mission Mode entry.

docs.text: Everything the driver reads comes from the chip over the bus, so the data read is what a noisy cable, a wrong part or a broken chip controls. tests/fuzz/fuzz_tle92466ed.cpp lets libFuzzer choose a configuration, then up to 1024 driver calls, and on every bus transfer what the bus does: pass it to the model, fail it, flip bits of the reply or replace it. Between calls it can change the chip: another version, an unprogrammed OTP, INIT_DONE that never comes, events that cannot be cleared, supply, clock, channel and data faults, the Critical Fault state, a refused Mission Mode, time passing, a brown-out. After every call it checks the driver's promises and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks: a failed call returns an Error the enum defines and T{} ; before EnsureInitialized() no call makes a transfer; InvalidArgument and WrongState mean nothing was sent; UnexpectedReset leaves the driver uninitialised; a programmed setpoint is inside the operating range and is what GetCurrentSetpoint() reports; feedback is a duty of at most 100 % over a measurement period; every transfer is one 32-bit frame with both buffers, and every log line is a non-empty plain-text message. # libFuzzer needs Clang (on macOS, Homebrew's LLVM) cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DTLE92466ED_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DTLE92466ED_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_tle92466ed ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_tle92466ed -max_total_time = 120 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_tle92466ed The same file also builds without libFuzzer as fuzz_replay_fuzz_tle92466ed , and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_tle92466ed/ on GCC and Clang ( tle92466ed_fuzz_tle92466ed_corpus ): the seeds, and every input that ever broke a promise (name it regress-* ), so a fixed bug stays fixed. CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request, from the seeds plus a corpus it keeps between runs (job Host quality / fuzz ).

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms, causes and fixes, cheapest check first. Section numbers refer to the datasheet, Rev. 1.2. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Infineon IFX-ntz1491827137291 1.2: Supplies, VIO_SEL and the power-on reset: 4.1.1 TDS_Power Supply, p. 14 Voltage monitoring and the VBAT thresholds: 4.1.2 TDS_Voltage monitoring; Equation 1, p. 14 Reset State, Config Mode, Mission Mode and Critical Fault: 4.3.1 TDS_IC Operation states; Figure 4, p. 19 Open load or short to ground, thresholds and warning: 4.9.2 TDS_Open Load/Short to Ground (OLSG); 4.9.3 TDS_OLSG Warning, p. 34 Register and OTP ECC, the self-test: 4.9.7 TDS_Register/OTP ECC; 4.9.8 TDS_Built in Self Test (BIST), p. 39 Average current, duty cycle and VBAT feedback: 4.10.2 TDS_Average feedback values; Equations 18 to 22, p. 41 The reply pipeline, frames and reply status: 5.2.1 TDS_Data flow; 5.2.3 SPI frame definition, p. 50 Identity, ICVID and CHIPID: 5.3.2.19 Version Register; 5.3.2.24 Unique Chip Identification Number Register 0, p. 75 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . GetBusDiagnostics() counts frames, retries, rejected replies and resyncs, and GetLastReply() holds the last 32-bit word read: log both while you look for a bus problem. EnsureInitialized returns Bus ¶ The port reported a failure: its EnsureInitialized() , a Transfer() or a GpioSet() returned false . Check that your port's EnsureInitialized() returns true on its own (log it). Check the bus and control pins in your port against the board. With a logic analyser, check that the first frames appear on the bus: an ICVID read (0x..C00200), then FB_STAT reads. EnsureInitialized returns NoDevice ¶ MISO read all zeros, all ones, or exactly the frame just sent. Nothing drives SO, or MOSI reaches MISO. GetLastReply() Likely cause Fix 0x00000000 VIO missing (SO is powered from VIO), the chip held in reset, SO not connected Check VIO, RESN high after the start, SO continuity 0xFFFFFFFF SO floating with a pull-up, or the chip unpowered Check VDD and VIO, CSN reaching pin 5 The frame sent MOSI and MISO shorted, or SO not soldered with MOSI coupled in Check the board EnsureInitialized returns Crc or ReplyMismatch ¶ Frames arrive, but not intact or not in step. The chip shifts SO on the rising SCK edge and samples SI on the falling edge: SPI mode 1 (section 5.1.1). Mode 0 typically gives Crc ; a shared bus that interleaves another transfer gives ReplyMismatch . Check CSN high time between frames (600 ns minimum, Table 18), lower the clock, and make sure no other code sends frames to this chip during a driver call. EnsureInitialized returns Timeout ¶ INIT_DONE in FB_STAT did not read 1 within Config::init_timeout_us (section 4.2.1): the clock or the logic is not ready. Check VDD (4.5 V to 5.5 V), RESN released, and with an external clock the CLK signal and Config::external_clock_khz . EnsureInitialized returns DeviceIdMismatch or DeviceFault ¶ DeviceIdMismatch : ICVID did not read manufacturer 0xC1 with version 0xFC (A11) or 0xFE (A13) (section 5.3.2.19): another part, or another design step this driver does not know. DeviceFault : OTP_VIRGIN is set, the chip's trim was never programmed (section 4.9.7: "this bit must always be 0"); GetStartupFaults() shows it. Replace the part. EnsureInitialized returns WriteMismatch ¶ GLOBAL_CONFIG did not read back what was written: the chip did not take a Config Mode write. Check that nothing else drives the chip and that MOSI reaches SI (reads alone work without it). EnterMissionMode returns MissionBlocked ¶ A fault of Figure 4 holds the chip in Config Mode. ReadStatus() says which kind, ReadFaults() which flag: Flag Likely cause Fix VioUndervoltage or VioOvervoltage Config::vio does not match the board (reset value 5 V) Set Config::vio to V3V3 on a 3.3 V MCU VddUndervoltage VDD below 4.5 V Check the 5 V rail VbatUndervoltage No load supply, or vbat_uv_code too high Check VBAT; the threshold is 162 mV per count SpiWatchdog The SPI watchdog expired ReloadWatchdog() often enough; then ClearFaults() ClockFault The clock watchdog saw f_SYS out of range The CLK pin and the dividers CentralOtWarning , CentralOtError The die is hot Cooling, load current Then ClearFaults() and EnterMissionMode() again. A flag that sets again at once means the cause is still there. Calls return CriticalFault ¶ Every reply is a critical fault frame: the chip is in the Critical Fault state (section 4.3.1), after an internal supply fault or a clock that runs too fast. GetLastCriticalFault() holds the flags (section 5.2.3.5): bits 7, 6 and 5 are 1 when the 1V5, 2V5 and the ADC bandgap are fine, bits 4 to 0 are clock faults (too slow, too fast, digital clock too slow or too fast, watchdog reference missing). A flags byte of 0x00 almost always means VDD is missing. The driver accepts the state only from two critical fault frames in a row (one alone can be noise), then drives EN low and is uninitialised. Only RESN ( EnsureInitialized() with GpioSet() ) or a power cycle leaves the state. A channel does not switch on ¶ EnableChannel(..., Verify::ReadBack) returns WriteMismatch , or the current stays at 0: A latched fault keeps it off. After an OLSG, OL, SG, OC or OTE the chip keeps the channel disabled until the flag is cleared and EN_CH is set again (sections 4.9.2 to 4.9.6). An OFF-state diagnosis can also latch OL or SG on a channel that was disabled with a setpoint still set. ReadFaults() , fix the load, ClearChannelFaults() , enable again. Not in Mission Mode , or the chip left it (a supply or watchdog fault): EnableChannel() returns MissionBlocked ; ReadChannelControl() shows it. Setpoint 0 : in ON state the setpoint must not be 0 (section 4.9.1). EN low : ReadPinStatus().value.enable . A slave : drive the master of the pair. The current regulates badly or stalls ¶ PWM_REG_WARN or I_REG_WARN in ReadFaults() : the integrator hit its limit or its threshold went negative (sections 4.6.2.4, 4.6.2.5). Set icc.min_int_thresh above 1 (the preset uses 2) and keep icc.auto_limit above min_int_thresh + 3. The PWM frequency drifts: set a PWM target ( icc.period_mant ) within 110 Hz to 4 kHz and a controller gain. A setpoint step overshoots: leave Autolimit on ( icc.auto_limit_disable = false ). ReadChannelFeedback returns NotReady ¶ Every time : the measurement period is the dither period (section 4.4.2) and DITHER_CLK_DIV resets to 0, so with dither.mant = 0 the feedback never updates. Give the channel a dither reference clock ( CurrentControlChannel() sets 1 ms), even with no dither amplitude. Sometimes : no new period since the last read; read at most once per measurement period. The channel must be enabled with a setpoint above 0 in Mission Mode, with EN high. Calls return UnexpectedReset ¶ POR_event or RES_event read 1 in an FB_STAT anchor after the start-up had cleared them: the chip reset since the driver started it, usually a brown-out on VDD or a RESN glitch. The driver is uninitialised again; EnsureInitialized() configures it. If it repeats, check the supply, its decoupling and RESN. Reads return Crc now and then ¶ Single corrupted replies point at signal integrity: lower the bus clock, shorten the wires, add a ground next to the clock line. The driver retries a read up to Config::max_retries times ( GetBusDiagnostics().retries ); a write is never retried, so its caller sees the error.
